evals.prompt: /cyoda:deploy — I want to run my shop app's cyoda on my laptop in Docker, just for me
evals.expected_output: Checks status and the local models, reads cyoda-manifest.json, recommends Docker Compose single-user (mock auth, loopback, labelled 'anyone who can reach these ports is admin'), writes deploy/cyoda/{compose.yaml, seed.sh, verify.sh, secrets-checklist.md} from the templates with image ghcr.io/cyoda/cyoda:${CYODA_VERSION:-0.8.4}, and ends with the ordered command list (up, health, seed, verify) without running any of them.

files._simulated/instance.md: Project root is /work/shop. cyoda-status.sh prints STATUS=connected PROFILE=default ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8080 ENV=development VERSION=0.8.4 BINARY_VERSION=0.8.4. cyoda-call.sh GET /model/ returns [{"modelName":"order","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"},{"modelName":"customer","modelVersion":1,"currentState":"LOCKED"}]. There is no deploy/ or ops/ dir. docker, helm and kubectl are installed. The developer picks Docker Compose single-user and says it is not production. They decline a profile.

assertions.text: Reads cyoda-manifest.json and lists order v1 and customer v1 as the entities to seed
Explains that single-user is mock auth on 127.0.0.1 and that anyone who can reach the ports is admin
Writes the files under deploy/cyoda/ because there is no existing deploy/ or ops/ dir
Writes compose.yaml (from compose.single-user.yaml), seed.sh, verify.sh and secrets-checklist.md into that dir
Ends with commands in this order: docker compose up, health check on /api/health, seed.sh with --manifest and --env development, verify.sh
Names at least one `cyoda help` section it relied on (e.g. run RUN MODES or PORT LAYOUT) rather than asserting facts from memory
Does not mention Cyoda Cloud
Every hand-off is phrased 'next, type `/cyoda:<skill>`' with a reason; it never says it will invoke or run another skill itself
Does not run docker, docker compose, helm, kubectl or openssl, and does not run seed.sh or verify.sh; it only writes files and lists the commands

evals.prompt: /cyoda:deploy — we need a shared cyoda instance for the team on our staging VM, staging.shop.example.com

It records CYODA_COMPUTE_GRPC_ENDPOINT=staging.shop.example.com:9090 in the checklist. It doesn't generate keys.

evals.prompt: /cyoda:deploy — put it on our Kubernetes cluster with Helm
evals.expected_output: Reads `cyoda help helm` (VALUES, SECRETS PROVISIONING, INSTALL / UPGRADE / UNINSTALL) and asks namespace, Postgres and routing. Installs from the published repo (helm repo add cyoda https://cyoda.github.io/cyoda-go), not ./deploy/helm/cyoda, noting help's 'unpublished, 0.1.0' is outdated (cyoda-go#684 item A). Writes deploy/cyoda/values.yaml from the template: postgres/jwt/hmac/metrics/bootstrap existingSecrets, bootstrap.clientId shop-deployer (#684 item D), gateway.parentRefs prod-gateway in gateway-system with hostnames api.shop.example.com and grpc.shop.example.com (#684 item G), ingress block removed, replicas/HPA/migrate at chart defaults, no placeholders left. Writes seed.sh, verify.sh and a Helm secrets checklist (cyoda-jwt, cyoda-bootstrap, cyoda-pg, cyoda-hmac, cyoda-metrics-bearer in namespace shop, no values, CYODA_COMPUTE_GRPC_ENDPOINT grpc.shop.example.com:443). Ends with the ordered commands: namespace + secrets, helm repo add/update and the chart whose appVersion is 0.8.4 via helm search | jq, helm install cyoda cyoda/cyoda --version ... -f deploy/cyoda/values.yaml -n shop, health on https://api.shop.example.com/api/health, seed, kubectl port-forward svc/cyoda 19091:9091 (not local 9091, which the local cyoda-go holds), a bounded wait, verify, then the forward stopped. Runs none of them; hands off to /cyoda:auth for the token script.

There is no deploy/ or ops/ dir. docker, helm and kubectl are installed. The developer picks Helm on Kubernetes, namespace shop, and says it is staging, not production. They have a managed Postgres the cluster can reach. The cluster runs Gateway API: Gateway prod-gateway in namespace gateway-system, which admits routes from all namespaces. assertions.text: Reads `cyoda help helm` sections (e.g. VALUES, SECRETS PROVISIONING, INSTALL / UPGRADE / UNINSTALL) and names the ones it used

Uses the published chart: `helm repo add cyoda https://cyoda.github.io/cyoda-go` and `cyoda/cyoda`, not `./deploy/helm/cyoda` or a packaged 0.1.0 tgz, and does not repeat help's claim that the chart is unpublished

Picks the chart version as the one whose appVersion is 0.8.4 (helm search repo cyoda/cyoda --versions with jq), and the install is `helm install cyoda cyoda/cyoda --version <that version> -f deploy/cyoda/values.yaml -n shop`
deploy/cyoda/values.yaml sets postgres.existingSecret and jwt.existingSecret, plus existingSecret for the HMAC, metrics bearer and bootstrap client secrets, and contains no secret value
values.yaml sets bootstrap.clientId (e.g. shop-deployer), and the seed command uses that client id

values.yaml enables the gateway with parentRefs naming prod-gateway in gateway-system and hostnames api.shop.example.com (http) and grpc.shop.example.com (grpc); ingress is not enabled; no `<PLACEHOLDER>` is left
replicas and autoscaling stay at chart defaults (1, disabled) and the migration Job is left on

secrets-checklist.md keeps only the Helm section, naming each Kubernetes Secret (cyoda-jwt, cyoda-bootstrap, cyoda-pg, cyoda-hmac, cyoda-metrics-bearer) in namespace shop and what reads it, with no values, and CYODA_COMPUTE_GRPC_ENDPOINT grpc.shop.example.com:443

Ends with commands in this order: create namespace and secrets, helm repo add/update and chart lookup, helm install, health on https://api.shop.example.com/api/health, seed.sh with --env development, verify.sh

Checks /readyz on the admin port 9091 through `kubectl port-forward` to a non-default local port (e.g. svc/cyoda 19091:9091, CYODA_ADMIN_URL=http://localhost:19091), not local 9091 (the local cyoda-go's admin port) and not through the Gateway; waits until the forward answers before verify.sh and stops the forward afterwards

evals.prompt: /cyoda:deploy — Helm on our k8s cluster. We run ingress-nginx there, there's no Gateway API
evals.expected_output: Takes the Ingress route: values.yaml has gateway.enabled false (not left on with empty parentRefs, cyoda-go#684 item G) and ingress.enabled true with className nginx, http.host cyoda.internal.example.com, grpc.host cyoda-grpc.internal.example.com and TLS Secret internal-tls for both, keeping the chart's gRPC backend-protocol annotation. Commands use the published repo, the chart whose appVersion is 0.8.4, helm install ... -n cyoda, health on https://cyoda.internal.example.com/api/health, seed, and verify with /readyz through kubectl port-forward from local 19091 to the admin port 9091. Runs none of them.
